title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 111: Ambergris: Floating Gold of the Oceans
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 111 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Ambergris: Floating Gold of the Oceans

Paragraph 1. For thousands of years, people walking along ocean beaches sometimes found a strange grey or white lump called ambergris. It looked like old wax or soft stone. Long ago, nobody knew where it came from. Arab traders thought it came from holes under the sea. Old Chinese stories claimed it was dry saliva from coastal dragons. Even though it looked ugly, people paid high prices for it to use in medicine and fine perfume.

Paragraph 2. In the 1800s, whale hunters finally learned that ambergris grows inside the stomachs of sperm whales. These giant whales dive deep into the ocean to eat huge squid. The whale digests the soft squid meat easily, but sharp squid beaks cannot melt inside the stomach. Usually the whale throws them up. Sometimes, sharp pieces enter the lower gut and hurt it, so the whale wraps them in a thick oily material that grows into ambergris.

Paragraph 3. Most whales do not die from this lump; they simply pass it out into the ocean with their waste. Fresh ambergris is soft, black, and smells very bad. However, after floating on the sea for many years, salty water and bright sunlight change the soft black lump into a hard silver-grey stone. Its terrible smell slowly turns into a sweet, earthy scent.

Paragraph 4. Good white ambergris can cost over $20,000 per kilogram because of a chemical called ambrein. Ambrein helps luxury perfumes stay on human skin for many hours. Historically, King Charles II of England loved to grate ambergris onto his breakfast eggs. Today, in the United States, it is completely illegal to buy, sell, or keep any ambergris, even if you find it on a beach. In Europe, however, selling beach ambergris is still legal.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "Old Chinese stories claimed it was dry saliva from coastal dragons."
Đoạn 2: "...sharp squid beaks cannot melt inside the stomach."
Đoạn 3: "...salty water and bright sunlight change the soft black lump..."
Đoạn 4: "...loved to grate ambergris onto his breakfast eggs."

q5.text: Ambergris is produced inside the stomachs of giant squid.

steps: Đoạn 2: Nó hình thành trong bụng cá nhà táng (sperm whales), không phải trong bụng mực khổng lồ.

q6.text: Fresh ambergris has a sweet flower smell as soon as it leaves the whale.

steps: Đoạn 3: Lúc mới ra ngoài nó màu đen, mềm và rất hôi (smells very bad).

q7.text: People in the United States are allowed to sell ambergris found on beaches.

steps: Đoạn 4: Ở Mỹ hoàn toàn bị cấm (completely illegal), kể cả đồ nhặt được trên biển.

q8.text: King Charles II paid more money for ambergris than for his palace.

steps: Đoạn 4: Chỉ nói vua thích ăn trứng với long diên hương, không so sánh tiền mua với cung điện.
